verdict: Ametek's sales rose 17% to a record $2.22B and profit set a record too, as both of its instrument businesses grew at double-digit rates and recent acquisitions chipped in.

kpis.label: Operating cash flow
kpis.note: Up 27%; free cash flow was 124% of net income

segments.name: Electronic Instruments (EIG)
segments.note: Precision instruments for aerospace, power, industrial and research markets — a record $1.44B, up 16%, helped by acquisitions.

segments.name: Electromechanical (EMG)
segments.note: Motors, pumps, interconnects and engineered materials — a record $778M in the quarter.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling products and running the company — kept to about a tenth of sales.

otherDetail: Interest and other non-operating items cost $63M, net — mostly interest on Ametek's debt.

takeaways.title: A record quarter, and guidance raised
takeaways.text: Sales rose 17% to a record $2.22B and GAAP profit rose to a record $426M. Management raised its full-year outlook after the strong quarter, citing broad-based organic growth plus contributions from recent acquisitions.

takeaways.title: Electronic Instruments did the heavy lifting
takeaways.text: EIG sales rose 16% to a record $1.44B with segment operating income of $407M. During the quarter Ametek also closed its acquisition of Indicor Instrumentation, adding another group of industrial technology businesses.

takeaways.title: Profit turned into cash, and then some
takeaways.text: Operating cash flow rose 27% to $561M, and free cash flow (cash left after buying equipment) equaled 124% of net income — the company collected more cash than its accounting profit, a sign of disciplined working capital.

oneTimers: Adjusted results add back $0.36 per share of acquisition-related intangible amortization and deal/integration costs, taking adjusted EPS to $2.21 versus the $1.85 GAAP figure — the business itself was not changed by these items.
